cells.tense: You're tending something that's growing here, and your hand doesn't have to close around it.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're carrying reach its own end, and let the end be enough. Not more tending — just the open hand.
cells.core:
You're growing something and you're not squeezing it. You give it what it needs, you wait, you don't force the outcome onto your own schedule. When you can hold a person through a hard week and still let yourself sleep, that's this working — the strength stays open instead of hardening over what it's protecting. The roots take because nothing is being gripped.

What opens up is room. When you let something finish without rushing in to rescue it, you can keep carrying the rest without carrying it heavier — because you're not also hauling around the fear of how it might turn out. The load gets lighter the moment the grip loosens.
cells.sheetLine: You grow things by tending, not by forcing — and it works.
cells.verb: Tending what's growing — giving it the conditions it needs without forcing how it turns out
cells.place: Where you carry what has to be carried, steady under weight without going hard

cells.tense: You're already out in a future that hasn't happened, holding it up before it arrives.
cells.ask: Stay with what's in front of you today. Let one worry stay unanswered, and do just the next ordinary thing.
cells.core:
You can carry someone through their worst week and still let them be the one who says what the week was. You can hold the weight and let the shape of it stay theirs, and the holding costs you less than the watching did — the strength is in the staying, not in the steering.

Right now you're carrying people long before they've asked. You've made yourself responsible for how it lands, and the care has turned into control, the keeping-safe into keeping-close. What you're holding can't breathe — and neither can you. The grip you call protection is doing the exhausting, not the load.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the whole outcome before anyone handed it to you.

cells.tense: You're standing in a doorway you already passed through, waiting for something to begin.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you actually want to see grow and give it one honest hour this week. Let wanting it be reason enough.
cells.core:
You can stand in the middle of something unfinished and still want to stay. You put care into one small thing and let it matter that you did — and the wanting itself feels allowed, not indulgent. That's what the holding is for when it's working: staying with a thing while it's still becoming.

Nothing's growing and you've decided that's simply how you are. The care is in you — you can see it in what you keep alive for other people — but you won't point it at anything of your own. From the outside it looks like independence. From the inside it's empty.
cells.sheetLine: You've kept your care flowing and given it nothing of your own to land on.

cells.tense: You're already the one holding it up, and you talk about it as though it were assigned.
cells.ask: Tell one person that a thing you do every day for them was your choice. Then let one piece of it go.
cells.core:
You can hold a whole household steady and still know the holding as yours — that's what this looks like when it's working. You carry what's heavy, and you don't pretend the carrying just happened to you, and the weight stays yours to set down when its time is done.

People count on you and you carry it, and you'd say it's just what has to be done. The tending is real and it's doing the work, holding things together, and the choosing behind it goes unnamed. Your own choice keeps getting filed as somebody else's arrangement.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying it like it was assigned. The choice is yours to claim.
